scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

One regional narrative spans Indigenous, Spanish, English/British colonial and independent periods. The imported 1920 start is map coverage, not Jamaica’s founding or independence. No new successor edges are inferred.

The British Museum catalogue supplies an updated scientific wood date, approximately 1000 to 1150, and a narrower catalogue range. The card uses the broad updated range rather than the older 15th-to-16th-century attribution retained in a quoted catalogue entry. Reported 1792 cave discovery is not a controlled excavation or a date for manufacture; no precise original ceremonial use is asserted.

New Street terrestrial excavations include material from before and after the 1692 earthquake. Their eighteenth-century pottery is not mislabelled as coming from the underwater kitchen sealed in 1692. Neither artifact group identifies all island households.

The Thornton inventories privilege property holders. The quoted toilet chair is documented in Port Royal; the Colonial Williamsburg object explains the furniture type only. No claim that the latter object came from Jamaica or that the particular Jamaican chair survives is made. The person responsible for waste removal is unknown.

Moore Town’s rituals and communication are not treated as universal Maroon practices. No sacred language, medicinal recipe or unsupported therapeutic efficacy is reproduced. UNESCO’s general treaty date is not used to resolve differences between individual Maroon treaties.

The Seacole biography has inconsistent middle-name spellings and a date-of-birth assertion that is unnecessary here. Only the account of mother-daughter learning and lodging-house care is used. The page does not imply that every historical treatment was effective.

The National Library and JIS differ on Ring Ding’s exact broadcast years. This card omits endpoints and does not confuse the span of an archive series with the broadcast run. Children’s participation and Bennett’s language advocacy are supported directly.

UNESCO’s reggae and Moore Town entries and the college letter were read in indexed form after direct access returned a JavaScript challenge. The relevant college letter was fully available in the indexed result. British Museum direct access returned 403; its full relevant catalogue passage was indexed. These limitations are not described as successful direct access.

The JIS history page contains dated racial stereotypes, total-extinction language about Indigenous people and errors concerning the slave-trade act, railway ownership, federation member count and Maroon-war chronology. None of these are reproduced. Only the supported broad colonial sequence, 1834/1838 distinction and 1944 election are used. The opening 1000 phase is a selected window for the wooden figures, not an island-wide polity or first settlement.
These new claims have been source-checked by their author and await independent historical review.

identityEvidence.assessment: Both outlines locate Jamaica south of Cuba. This establishes broad island identity, not precise historical coastlines or the extent of colonial dependencies.
